appraisal_events.evidence: princesse de Parme s'écria à la pensée qu'elle pourrait trouver Mme de Guermantes bête, et protesta éperdument que rien ne pouvait faire déchoir la duchesse du rang qu'elle occupait dans son admiration
appraisal_events.explanation: Even the mere suggestion that the duchesse might seem foolish provokes an emphatic protest from the princesse de Parme, who insists nothing could lower her from the very high esteem in which she holds her; the narrator reports this fervent deference as genuine, confirming the duchesse's exalted local standing.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Denier ! inopportun ! comme elle s'exprime bien ! » dit le duc avec une ironie feinte et pour faire admirer la duchesse.
appraisal_events.explanation: Although the duke's tone is outwardly ironic, the narrator explicitly states his purpose is to showcase Oriane's clever expression and win her admiration from others, so the underlying movement is a genuine elevation of the duchesse's wit rather than mockery of her.

status_effects.explanation: The princesse de Parme's frantic insistence that nothing could lower the duchesse in her admiration confirms Oriane's very high local standing in this exchange.
The duke's remark, though delivered with feigned irony, is explicitly framed by the narrator as designed to make others admire Oriane's clever way of speaking.

ambiguities: The identity of the unnamed 'cruche de cousine' to whom Oriane compares herself is not resolvable from the passage; she is Basin's cousin and only loosely related to Oriane, but no confident match to a reference-sheet entity is warranted, so she is omitted from characters_present.
